label: flash-kapitsa
note: Kapitsa's default settings for this model: the model's own MTP head at Kapitsa's default depth for Flash-Next (2 from 95fbcd6, 1 before; --spec not passed), --dflash none naming the absence of a block drafter (none exists for this model). The folder is Nace AI's MLX pack of Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next @ de4b8e4d (nace-ai/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-MLX-4bit: routed experts, GDN, shared experts and LM head 4-bit g64, hyper-connections and attention 6-bit g64, router, indexer, n-gram projections and embedding 8-bit g64; 71.4 GB on the GPU, 1.5 GB MTP head, the 32.0 GB n-gram table 4-bit g32 in ple.safetensors, memory-mapped and read from the SSD row by row, not in GPU memory). --slots 1 for parity with the others' single sequence. Reference prompt lengths 4133 / 16286: the corpus prompts through this model's tokenizer and chat template (transformers apply_chat_template, enable_thinking false, 8 nonces each: 4132-4135 / 16283-16288), the same as Qwen3.6 / Qwen3.8's.

label: flash-kapitsa-plain
note: The same server with --spec 0: plain one-token decoding, for comparison with the other engines' plain configurations. Everything else as flash-kapitsa.

label: flash-mlxvlm
version_cmd: import importlib.metadata as m; print('mlx-vlm', m.version('mlx-vlm'), 'mlx', m.version('mlx'))
note: mlx-vlm 0.7.8 (the latest release; git main @ 73d366e adds nothing for qwen4_exp) on the same folder Kapitsa reads: the pack follows mlx-vlm's qwen4_exp parameter layout, so its sanitize is a no-op, and its ple_storage manifest makes mlx-vlm serve the n-gram table's rows from a memory map of ple.safetensors (cache_rows 0), as Kapitsa does. Automatic prefix caching on (APC_ENABLED=1, in memory only), mlx-vlm's own switch for reusing a conversation's prefix in follow-up turns (off by default); 2048-token prefill steps (its default, stated); one sequence at a time. The request's model id is the path the server was started with.

label: flash-mlxvlm-mtp
note: As flash-mlxvlm, with the model's own MTP head as the drafter (--draft-kind mtp; mlx-vlm 0.7.8's qwen4_exp_mtp drafter). Passing the pack folder itself as --draft-model fails in 0.7.8 ('Expected shape (2560, 320) but received shape (2560, 640) for parameter fc_embedding.weight'): its MTP splitter keeps the source's per-module quantization keys ('mtp.fc_embedding': 8-bit), but the drafter's modules are named without the 'mtp.' prefix, so the head's 8-bit and 6-bit layers are built as 4-bit. --draft-model therefore names a drafter folder made from the pack's own MTP head (qwen3.8-flash-next-4bit-mlxvlm-mtp: the 74 tensors of mtp.safetensors byte for byte, prepared by mlx-vlm's own Qwen4ExpMTPSplitter, with the config's per-module precisions named by the drafter's paths). Block size 4: the fastest of the drafter's default and 2-5 in smoke tests on this Mac (2 runs each, 4K prompt; T = 0.6 / greedy tok/s: default (adaptive, configured block 2) 74.5 / 82.4, block 2 66.2 / 67.1, 3 77.4 / 83.5, 4 80.4 / 87.5, 5 77.5 / 79.4).

label: flash-omlx
note: oMLX 0.7.1rc1 (the latest release) on the same folder Kapitsa reads: oMLX routes model type qwen4_exp to its vendored mlx-vlm qwen4_exp model (with its own QSA kernels), which reads the pack as stored (its parameter layout is mlx-vlm's). oMLX keeps the n-gram table resident in memory for this folder (log: 'Qwen4-Exp PLE mode ...: resident'; it switches to reading rows from the SSD only for checkpoints above 70% of RAM), so its memory includes the 32 GB table that Kapitsa and mlx-vlm map from the SSD. MTP off in its model settings; flash-omlx-mtp is its MTP configuration. Cache flags as in omlx.json.

label: flash-omlx-mtp
note: oMLX's Lightning MTP (its built-in MTP path) with the pack's own MTP head, which oMLX finds through model.safetensors.index.json (mtp.safetensors). Depth: fixed 3 (mtp_fixed_depth), the fastest in smoke tests on this Mac (2 runs each, 4K prompt; T = 0.6 / greedy tok/s): adaptive (oMLX's default, up to 3) 94.3 / 91.7; fixed 1 86.6 / 91.9; fixed 2 102.7 / 104.8; fixed 3 109.7 / 111.3; fixed 4 101.3 / 99.7; fixed 5 95.2 / 101.0; the same folder without MTP 56.5 / 56.6.

label: flash-omlx-oq4e
note: oMLX on its author's own quantization of the model: Jundot/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-oQ4e-mtp @ c4ddfb54 (oQ4e, oMLX 0.7.1's mixed-precision quantizer with an importance matrix: routed experts 4-bit g64, the n-gram table 4-bit g32, other layers 5-8-bit at g64 / g128, embedding and LM head 8-bit; 4.72 bits per weight, 106.3 GB with the MTP head; the most downloaded MLX conversion of the model). Its sizes match the pack's (language model 71.9 vs 71.4 GB, the same 32.0 GB table, MTP head 1.48 vs 1.51 GB). MTP off; flash-omlx-oq4e-mtp is its MTP configuration. Cache flags as in omlx.json.

label: flash-omlx-oq4e-mtp
display: oMLX + MTP, oQ4e (Lightning MTP, fixed depth 2)
note: oMLX's Lightning MTP on Jundot/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-oQ4e-mtp @ c4ddfb54 with its embedded MTP head (as flash-omlx-oq4e otherwise). Depth: fixed 2, the fastest in smoke tests on this Mac (2 runs each, 4K prompt; T = 0.6 / greedy tok/s): adaptive (default, up to 3) 108.2 / 97.6; fixed 2 110.7 / 105.6; fixed 3 104.7 / 101.2; fixed 4 106.0 / 96.0.

label: flash-llamacpp
note: llama.cpp v0.7.0 (build b11669, the latest release; qwen4exp since b10660, its MTP since b11330) on ggml-org's official GGUF of the model: ggml-org/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF @ 0a61d2b8, IQ4_NL (two files, 102.05 GB: routed experts and the MoE-side hyper-connections IQ4_NL, attention, Gated DeltaNet, shared experts, embedding and LM head Q8_0, routers F32; the n-gram table, Q4_0, is in the GGUF and llama.cpp memory-maps it and reads its rows on the CPU, so it stays outside the process footprint even with -lm none). The closest of the GGUFs that fit this Mac's disk to the pack's size and format: ggml-org's other quantizations are Q2_K (83.1 GB) and Q8_0 (162.6 GB); unsloth's UD-IQ4_XS (93.7 GB) is smaller with mixed 3-4-bit tensors, UD-Q4_K_XL (111.3 GB) and Q4_K_M GGUFs (119-120 GB) did not fit beside the other weights. Settings as llama.cpp.json: one 32K slot, all layers on the GPU, flash attention, 2048-token batches, -lm none so the weights count in the footprint, the chat template inside the GGUF with --jinja, --min-p 0, prompt cache and 32 context checkpoints (the Gated DeltaNet layers' state for prefix reuse).

label: flash-llamacpp-mtp4
note: MTP speculative decoding with the model's MTP head, which ggml-org ships as a separate GGUF next to the trunk (mtp-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Q4_0.gguf, 2.20 GB, the file llama.cpp's own -hf download pairs with the 4-bit trunks). n-max 4: the fastest at T = 0.6 of 1-6 in smoke tests on this Mac (2 runs each, 4K prompt; T = 0.6 / greedy tok/s: n-max 1 65.7 / 67.1, 2 82.6 / 86.0, 3 (llama-server's default) 85.5 / 91.1, 4 94.7 / 97.3, 5 89.0 / 100.9, 6 83.7 / 96.2).

label: flash-ollama-mlx
display: Ollama MLX runner (official NVFP4 tag, MTP)
log_grep: starting runner|ollama runner|mlx runner is ready
note: Ollama 0.40.6 (the latest release) with its MLX runner on the official tag Ollama serves on Apple silicon, qwen3.8-flash-next:125b-mlx (= :125b-a6b-nvfp4, manifest sha256:c7b96ffe21af; NVFP4, 104.85 GB with the n-gram table, the MTP head and the vision tower; requires 0.33.1), through a derived tag that only sets num_ctx 32768 (nace/qwen3.8-flash-next:125b-mlx-32k: FROM the official tag plus PARAMETER num_ctx 32768, no data copied), because the tag's own parameters set num_ctx 262144, which overrides OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH. A dedicated `ollama serve` on :8310 over its own store (OLLAMA_MODELS). The runner's built-in MTP with its adaptive depth (no knobs; 3 extra warm-up decodes). Requests override sampling as for every engine. On this Mac the runner cannot read the 4K or 16K prompt: every such request fails with 'mlx runner failed: panic: mlx: [METAL] Command buffer execution failed: Insufficient Memory' (the runner holds about 98-100 GiB, and the prefill's buffers push it past the 107.5 GiB Metal working-set limit); decode and tool calls work.

label: flash-ollama-gguf
note: Ollama 0.40.6's GGUF runner (its bundled llama.cpp) on the official GGUF tag qwen3.8-flash-next:125b-a6b-q4_K_M (manifest sha256:f79436a1cc83; Q4_K_M, 119.15 GB plus a 0.91 GB vision projector; requires 0.33.3). The tag carries no MTP draft (unlike Ollama's qwen3.6 / qwen3.8 -mtp tags), so Ollama runs it without speculation. Settings as ollama.json: a dedicated `ollama serve` on :8312 over the same store, 32K context (OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH; this tag sets no num_ctx), one slot, flash attention on.

label: flash-mtplx
note: MTPLX 2.12.2 on its author's Bare-Speed pack (Youssofal/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-MTPLX-Bare-Speed @ 4285a4a0, 106.3 GB) at the settings its mtplx_runtime.json recommends (profile turbo, MTP depth 3). The larger Optimized-Speed pack (115.1 GB) was not run: it exceeds this Mac's GPU working-set limit (about 107.5 GiB).

label: flash-mlxserve-mtp
note: mlx-serve 26.10.2 on its vendor's Flash-Next pack for 128 GB Macs, the one the vendor recommends (ddalcu/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-MLX-Serve-iQ-MLX-4.7bpw @ a0e89db0; its 32 GB ngram_table.bin is the same file as in the vendor's mixed-4-8bit pack), with the pack's own MTP head (--mtp, as the pack's README says).
